cohort: 510,615 primiparous women with singleton pregnancies who gave birth in Denmark between 1997 and 2016.
finding: Primiparous women with pre-eclampsia had a lower rate of subsequent birth, but for those who did have another pregnancy, maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality were substantially improved despite a 1 in 6 risk of recurrent pre-eclampsia.
followup_time: variable, until subsequent birth, emigration, death, or end of study (December 2016)
gest_age: all gestational ages for singleton births; early-onset PE defined as birth <34 weeks
